symptom: `$R = UNION $L WITH $S` (and INTERSECT, SUBTRACT, EQUALS, `CONTAINS $S IN $L`) with a primitive variable as the operand that is not the list passed `check` and `exec`, and the build reported CE0023 "Selected variable 'S' must be of type Object or List." The same shape with an Object or List operand built clean.
file: mdl/executor/validate_list_operand_kinds.go checkListOperandKinds (MDL101), called from validate_microflow.go and validate_nanoflow.go after the primitive kinds are seeded. Tests: validate_list_operand_kinds_test.go; fixtures mdl-examples/bug-tests/list-operand-primitive(.fail).mdl
cause: The only CE0023 findings were the `contains` String overload (ledger #53), which the builder rewrites into a Change Variable; nothing judged the operand type of a list operation that really is one. The validators already had the kind of every parameter and declare (varKinds) and used it for MDL063 and the numeric-assignment rules, but not here.
insight: **When a code is in the field-hit list only because of an overload workaround, measure the general shape the workaround stands next to: the operand-type matrix was cheaper than guessing the boundary.** One project, one flow per case, `mx check -j` read per document (the `locations[].document-name` field, not the error object): 42 first-and-second-operand cases, then 25 more over Boolean, Decimal, DateTime, Long and enumeration. Result: for UNION, INTERSECT, SUBTRACT, EQUALS and CONTAINS the second operand being any primitive is CE0023 (7 types x 5 operations = 35 of 35, nanoflows the same), an Object or List there is clean (`union $L with $O` builds), a wrong FIRST operand is CE0097 and COUNT/SUM over a non-list is CE0013 (both left for their own rules; `range $S limit 2` was clean). Staging did not interfere because every flow was its own document. Visitor mapping to remember: `SUBTRACT $A FROM $B` and `CONTAINS $A IN $B` store the LIST in InputVariable and the other operand in SecondVariable. An enumeration parameter `LO.Color` is indistinguishable from an object at parse time, so it is silent (5 of 63 measured cases, listed in the PR); a declared `enum` variable is judged. Sweep: 1,317 repo .mdl files, 0 MDL101 hits. Control: stubbing the check fails 60 sub-tests; the String `contains` function still passes.
